transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Redwood: Maya Patel (AE), Ethan Ross (SE)
Horizon: Dr. Lina Gomez (CTO), Rajiv Shah (Lead SWE), Sophie Chen (DevOps), Alex (Data Scientist)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/decks/horizon-orient (deck), repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/horizon-quickstart (samples), benchmark sheet: https://sheets.redwood/horizon-bench (internal)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): quick walkthrough of SDK quickstart (py/ts), auth flow (API keys + KMS), console demo for model routing and Optimize suggestions, discussed hosted vs dedicated and VPC options; agreed to run benchmarks and share SOC2 + KMS details; pilot kickoff planned.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, uh thanks for joining, i'm maya patel from redwood, i'm the ae on this. um we've got about 50 minutes, i'd love to run through a quickstart, auth, console, and then ethan will show a short optimize/recommendation flow.
[00:18] Dr. Lina: great, thanks maya. our timebox is tight so if we could focus on integration blockers—vpc, kms, and perf—that'd be most useful.
[00:27] Maya: perfect, noted. quick intro round? ethan?
[00:31] Ethan: hi all, ethan ross, solutions eng. i'll do the demo parts and the benchmark plan.
[00:37] Rajiv: rajiv here, i lead platform engineering, will own sandbox setup and CI keys.
[00:41] Sophie: sophie, infra, will look at network and kms aspects.
[00:44] Alex: alex — data scientist, will bring sample prompts and eval sets.

[02:05] Maya: ok jumping in — first slide is 'quickstart flow'. two paths: hosted api (fastest), or private/dedicated (for higher throughput or strict residency). for your compliance needs, we usually recommend private deployment or dedicated with VPC peering, but we can start hosted sandbox to speed pilot.
[02:29] Dr. Lina: is the hosted path going to break our SOC2 posture? we can't send PHI without controls.
[02:36] Maya: good question — short answer: hosted can be used for PII-reduced testing; for PHI/regulatory you want private or dedicated with customer-managed KMS. we'll email the SOC2 scope doc after this.

[04:10] Ethan: now the SDK bit — two repos: python sample and typescript sample. show quick code. (screen) python snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.generate("summarize: ...")
[04:35] Ethan: you can also pass a key resolver for KMS rotation, e.g., call out to a local vault. our SDK supports GCP/AWS workload identity flows and a token refresh hook.
[05:02] Rajiv: wait — can you show env var pattern for CI? we prefer not to bake keys into images.
[05:08] Ethan: yeah we recommend ephemeral CI secrets, use the redwood console to create project-scoped keys with limited scopes and rotate via our API. example: REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT=proj-abc-...
[05:22] Sophie: how do we integrate with our AWS KMS? we have a managed HSM and strict key policies.
[05:28] Ethan: private deployments support using your KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we do envelope encryption where you keep the root key. for hosted we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS for key wrapping — but if you need on-prem HSM, private package is the option.

[07:50] Maya: switching to Console demo — where you create a sandbox project and generate keys, and then set routes. ethan will walk through Optimize suggestions after.
[08:03] Ethan: (screen) console->projects->quickstart. here you can see token/latency breakdown per route, and an Optimize tab that suggests batching size, quantization profiles and alternate cheaper models for similar output. you can 'apply' a suggested profile which creates an autoscaling config.
[08:40] Alex: quick q — the Optimize suggestions are deterministic? how do you measure quality impact?
[08:46] Ethan: good point — Optimize runs evaluations on your prompt set (you can upload a small eval) and reports delta in Rouge/bleu/semantic metrics plus sample completions. everything is auditable — there's an eval run id.

[10:12] Dr. Lina: on model fallbacks — if the primary model is down or overloaded, can we automatically route to a cheaper variant? we can't have downtime for triage.
[10:20] Ethan: yes, smart routing rules allow you to set a fallback chain; we support model variants with cheaper quantized versions. for strict latency SLOs you can pin to dedicated capacity and set fallback to a lower-cost but compatible variant.

[12:00] Rajiv: let's talk perf — p99 budgets. we aim for p99 < 350ms for single-turn summarization at 512 tokens. what would you expect on hosted?
[12:12] Ethan: it depends on model and sequence length. on our standard m-8a-family open model with 512, p99 is around 280-320ms in our hosted EU region; but you'll want to run a Horizon dataset benchmark to be sure. i'll run a 1k req bench using your prompts to measure token-cost and latency.
[12:36] Sophie: you'll need access to sample prompts and a sandbox key for that.
[12:40] Maya: action: sophie to provision sandbox key, ethan to run benchmark. noted.

[15:05] Ethan: quick demo of SDK error handling — example of a 429 backoff. SDK exposes retry hooks and will surface headers for rate limit reset. you can also set client.per_route_concurrency to tune batching.
[15:30] Rajiv: how does batching affect latency vs cost? we want to avoid added tail latency.
[15:37] Ethan: batching reduces per-token cost but increases tail latency; Optimize recommends batching config based on your request distribution. we also do smart prefix caching to reduce repeated token compute for similar prompt prefixes.

[19:10] Maya: briefly on network — VPC peering vs private link. sophie?
[19:18] Sophie: we prefer peering for high-throughput. what's redwood's recommendation?
[19:25] Ethan: both supported; peering is simple, private link is more firewall-friendly. for high throughput low-latency peering plus dedicated capacity tends to be best. we'll share sample CIDRs and peering steps in the checklist.

[22:40] Dr. Lina: licensing and cost structure — can you give an example for dedicated?
[22:46] Maya: dedicated is reserved capacity + usage; we can provide a sample TCO sheet (we will). for pilot we usually go hosted with a capped spend and then move to dedicated if throughput/cost warrants.

[25:00] Ethan: now a short walkthrough of Typescript quickstart — node example: import {RedwoodClient} from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}); await client.chat.send(...)
[25:20] Ethan: the TS client supports streaming via event emitters and transforms for tool-calling. we have express middleware for serverless environments that handles token introspection.
[26:02] Rajiv: do you have sample CI templates for rotating keys?
[26:09] Ethan: yes — in repo under .github/workflows we demonstrate using HashiCorp Vault + ephemeral role exchange. will share link.

[29:50] (brief cross-talk as screen loads)
[30:10] Maya: security review quick hits — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, retention policies. sophie any questions?
[30:21] Sophie: retention — how long do logs live and can we configure retention per project?
[30:27] Ethan: yes, retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private; hosted has default retention 90 days but we can offer extended retention as add-on. audit logs stream to your SIEM via our log forwarder.

[33:00] Dr. Lina: any red flags with our current infra? we run on AWS, EKS, have KMS, and strict egress rules.
[33:10] Ethan: should be fine — main items: sandbox key creation, VPC peering or private link, KMS wrap for keys if PHI, and a small bench to validate latency. we'll provide a checklist and a runbook for peering.

[36:40] Maya: okay let's demo Optimize briefly — i uploaded a small prompt set. ethan?
[36:46] Ethan: (console) Optimize suggests: increase batch size to 8 for this workload, try model quantized-2 for cheaper tokens, and apply prefix cache for identical headers. predicted cost savings ~18% with negligible quality drop according to our eval. you can click 'apply' and it will create a new route config and a canary rollout.
[37:30] Alex: if we apply a canary, can we route a % of traffic based on header or user id?
[37:36] Ethan: yes, routing supports header-based rules, sampling, and rollout windows. good for A/B.

[40:00] Rajiv: req for pilot: we'll need RBAC for project-level keys, separate keys for analytics vs prod. can you support scoped keys?
[40:08] Maya: yep, project-scoped + route-scoped keys are supported. we'll send a sample policy for keys.

[43:25] Sophie: about billing — can we get per-route cost breakdown?
[43:30] Ethan: yes, console shows token and request breakdown per route and per-model. we can also export usage to BigQuery.

[46:50] Dr. Lina: great, i'm comfortable with the approach. quick ask: can you run an end-to-end pilot where you try our exact prompt set and measure p50/p95/p99 and token-cost?
[46:59] Ethan: absolutely, that's the benchmark action item. i'll need a sandbox key and the prompt file.
[47:07] Dr. Lina: we'll share prompts after session.

[50:10] Maya: recap and next steps: (1) sophie provision sandbox key and CIDR info by 10/17, (2) ethan run benchmark and share sheet by 10/21, (3) maya share SOC2 + KMS notes and sample peering runbook by 10/16, (4) schedule pilot kickoff 10/23.
[50:40] Rajiv: sounds good. one more — can we get a quick cost estimate for a 3-month dedicated reserve?
[50:47] Maya: yes i'll loop finance and send an estimate.

[52:05] Alex: thanks all — quick nit: the TS streaming example had a small typo in the snippet, can you share the corrected snippet?
[52:11] Ethan: noted, will attach corrected snippet in follow-up email.
[53:00] Maya: thanks everyone; we'll follow up with notes and artifacts.
[53:10] (meeting ends)

Post-call notes (autogenerated): shared repo + deck; flagged security docs; agreed benchmark and pilot kickoff; items assigned in action_items.
